content.text: A duel is an engagement in personal combat between two characters.
Rulers have access to a Duel diplomatic action if they have War focus , membership in a Warrior Lodge , or a bloodline that "Enables dueling".
Unless the dueling game rule is set to "Unrestricted", the initiator must have one of the following reasons to challenge the target:

items.text: Foe (certain opinion modifiers toward the initiator, including "Cuckolded" and "Attempted Murder")
Target is Excommunicated ; initiator is Zealous and same religion
Target is Decadent ; initiator is Zealous and Muslim
Initiator has a mission to duel target ( Warrior Lodge quest)

content.text: Both characters must be in good shape to duel:

items.text: Duelers have NOT recently been in any duel (within 3 months)
Duelers do NOT have the character modifier Bedridden or Severe Illness
Duelers must each be at peace (for courtiers, this means that their liege must be at peace)

sections.heading: Challenge to duel for strong claim [1]

content.text: With the Holy Fury DLC, a tribal ruler can use a diplomatic action to challenge another tribal ruler to a duel over a strong claim . Both rulers must be independent or in the same realm, the claim must be over the defendant's primary title. Many of the other requirements and mechanics are the same as in duels for honor , as listed above.

If you lose a Strong Claim duel and die, and the winner is a member of your dynasty, you may switch play to the other character. This makes Strong Claim duels a potentially effective way to consolidate titles after a gavelkind split, at the price of culling dynasts.
If you are the current title holder, you have the choice of rejecting the duel, at the cost of getting Craven .

items.text: Germanic men may get an event suggesting they challenge a disliked character to a Holmgang . Opinion must be below -40. Possible opponents are the liege, any vassal, or any fellow vassal.
Confronting a spouse's lover may result in a duel.
As a method of suicide , you may challenge a rival to a duel that you intend to lose. Unlike other methods of suicide, this is considered an honorable death.
When attempting to establish a warrior lodge bloodline , you will face a series of increasingly difficult duels.
dueling one's love interest's spouse during the "Courtly Love" event chain [3]

content.text:
Since Crusader Kings II was developed over the better part of a decade, and the duel mechanic changed significantly over that time period, some duels use different code and thus a different mechanic to calculate the result.
Having high personal combat skill and an opponent with low personal combat skill usually makes better outcomes more likely though.

The process of the duels that have been updated to (or were created with) the Holy Fury duel mechanic, uses a scripted effect called "send_duel_result_event_effect" to determine the duel outcome.
This scripted effect makes use of a big random list to calculate the probabilities for the different outcomes of a duel and then randomly picks a result from the eligible ones. [4]
The following tables and explanations try to illuminate the way the game calculates the duel outcomes and thus what the respective probabilities of outcomes are.

sections.heading: Using Poison in the Duel (Intrigue Option) [10]

content.text: Duelists with at least 12 intrigue  (and the Holy Fury DLC ), can sometimes [18] use a special option to use poison during a duel.

This sets the character flag attacker_using_poison@event_target:combatant_2 for the attacker and/or the character flag defender_using_poison@event_target:combatant_1 for the defender, depending on which of the duelists chooses the option (i.e. attacker, defender or both).

If the opponent of a duelist trying to use poison either has at least as much intrigue as the poisoner or has a spymaster with that much intrigue, that likes them (opinion ≥ 15), then they get the character flag poison_can_fail_against@event_target:combatant_2 (if the poisoner is the attacker) or poison_can_fail_against@event_target:combatant_1 (if the poisoner is the defender) whichever is appropriate.
These poison_can_fail_against character flags negate a big part of the random list weights of the using_poison character flags .
Taking the option to use poison for a duel (that is not a duel for a claim) will change character traits in the following way:

items.text: If Deceitful and Brave , lose Brave
If Deceitful and not Brave , gain Craven

sections.heading: Example of Probability Calculation for Duel Outcomes

content.text: To illustrate the duel mechanic let's assume that your character with a personal combat skill of 70 has the war focus and is thus able to use the diplomatic action to challenge their rival with a personal combat skill of 50 to a duel (for honor).

Let's further assume that neither is weak nor craven , nor has any bloodlines, nor is a member of a warrior lodge.
Let's also assume, that the attacker uses a gun while the defender does not. But only the defender uses poison, but the attacker has high enough intrigue to get the possibility of countering it.

This eliminates all the "LEGENDARY BLOODLINES" outcomes (no warrior lodge means no legendary journey, which means no "has_character_flag = is_legendary_duel"), the "attacker/defender runs away" outcomes (neither the traits nor the bloodlines that can trigger those are there) and the "LETHAL/PRISON for defender (BATTLE ONLY)" outcome (the duel is not on a battlefield, thus no "has_character_flag = is_battlefield_duel"). [21]
Thus leaving only these outcomes:

Now that the eligibility of the duel outcomes is determined, let's calculate the duel_result_score (let's assume aside from the rivalry and the "no strong feelings" modifiers, there are no further extra bonuses):

duel_result_score = 50 (base) + 70 (personal combat skill of the attacker) - 50 (personal combat skill of the defender) + 6 (duelists are rivals) + 1 (attacker has no strong feelings) - 1 (defender has no strong feelings) = 76
That means that the duel_result_score falls within the range of the duel_result_score_great_trigger and the duel_result_score_high_group_trigger .
It's further necessary to convert the personal combat skill numbers to the appropriate ranges:
Personal combat skill of the attacker is 70 thus falls within the range of is_good_duelist_trigger and duelist_skill_is_medium_group_trigger .
Personal combat skill of the defender is 50 thus falls within the range of is_decent_duelist_trigger and duelist_skill_is_medium_group_trigger .
Now let's proceed to the calculation of the weight of the outcomes:
LETHAL for both: weight = 5 (base) = 5
LETHAL for attacker: weight = 5 (base) + 30 (defender is using poison) - 25 (poison can fail against attacker) = 10
LETHAL for defender: weight = 5 (base) + 5 (duel_result_score_high_group_trigger) + 30 (attacker has gun, defender does not) = 40
Attacker wounded someone: weight = 10 (base) + 60 (duel_result_score_great_trigger) + 60 (duel_result_score_high_group_trigger) = 130
Defender wounded someone: weight = 10 (base) = 10
Both wounded... (attacker wins?) -- "stalemates": weight = 5 (base) + 5 (duel_result_score_high_group_trigger) = 10
Both wounded... (defender wins?) -- "stalemates": weight = 5 (base) = 5
That means the total weight of all possible outcomes is 5 + 10 + 40 + 130 + 10 + 10 + 5 = 210 .
Which in turn means the probabilities for the different outcomes are:
LETHAL for both:
probability = 5/210 = 2.38%
LETHAL for attacker:
probability = 10/210 = 4.76%
LETHAL for defender:
probability = 40/210 = 19.05%
Attacker wounded someone:
probability = 130/210 = 61.90%
Defender wounded someone:
probability = 10/210 = 4.76%
Both wounded... (attacker wins?) -- "stalemates":
probability = 10/210 = 4.76%
Both wounded... (defender wins?) -- "stalemates":
probability = 5/210 = 2.38%
